entries.title: BinaryBot Home
entries.identity: The role-aware entry point into BinaryBot's Telegram interface.
entries.purpose: It identifies the current user context and provides safe navigation to the surfaces available in that context.
entries.pipeline_position: Telegram is a presentation and interaction layer over canonical runtime, control, and delivery subsystems.
controls: Owners may enter the governed Admin Control Surface.
consequences: Navigation changes only the visible Telegram page.
Opening a page does not change strategy, execution, distribution, or permissions.
limitations: The Home page is not proof that market data, signal generation, or broker execution is healthy.
Telegram is not a source of strategy truth.

entries.title: System Status
entries.identity: A read-only summary of the runtime evidence currently available to Telegram.
entries.purpose: It helps a human distinguish service state, market-data state, Telegram state, FSM state, recovery state, shadow mode, and broker-execution availability.
entries.pipeline_position: It consumes operational evidence; it does not create runtime or trading truth.
controls: Return to the previous page or Home.
consequences: Refresh requests a new snapshot but does not restart or mutate the system.
limitations: A healthy service does not prove profitable signals.
Telegram availability does not prove market-data freshness or broker execution.
UNKNOWN means sufficient evidence was not available; it must not be read as healthy or failed.
glossary: HEALTHY / RUNNING
The available operational evidence reports normal activity.
DEGRADED_SAFE
The system is restricted because required evidence or a dependency is impaired.
UNKNOWN
The interface cannot determine the state from sufficient canonical evidence.
SHADOW
The system may observe or evaluate, but this is not live broker execution.
BROKER DISABLED
No automatic broker trade execution is available through this runtime.

entries.title: Help
entries.identity: The role-scoped inventory of discoverable Telegram actions.
entries.purpose: It shows how to reach available surfaces without depending on remembered slash commands.
entries.pipeline_position: Help describes presentation routes; command authorization remains owned by the permission layer.
consequences: Reading Help never grants a role or permission.
limitations: A listed command may still require the configured admin context and an explicit permission.

entries.title: Admin Control Surface
entries.identity: The role-scoped launch surface for observing, diagnosing, controlling, and governing BinaryBot.
entries.purpose: It gives the Owner and authorized operators one navigable control environment while preserving the authority of each canonical subsystem.
entries.pipeline_position: It sits above specialized operational, decision, distribution, research, identity, health, governance, and audit panels.
controls: Open only the panels visible to the current role.
Use governed mutation controls only where a separate permission check allows them.
consequences: Opening a panel is read-only.
A material control may change future governed behavior and must remain permission-checked and auditable.
limitations: The Admin surface displays and controls canonical truths; it does not redefine strategy or execution truth.
Owner authority still acts through governed interfaces and audit rules.

entries.title: Operations
entries.identity: The operational-state and governed-recovery area of the control plane.
entries.purpose: It brings together engine state, diagnostics, strategy parameters, coverage, restrictions, and recovery evidence needed for day-to-day operation.
entries.pipeline_position: It observes runtime and dependency evidence and may invoke only explicitly governed operational controls.
controls: Open Strategy Parameters and Symbols & Coverage.
Use future operational controls only when they are implemented, authorized, and audited.
consequences: Inspection is read-only.
A future pause, freeze, recovery, or routing control can restrict forward behavior and must produce audit evidence.
limitations: Operations health does not prove signal quality or profitability.
The current page must not imply that unimplemented freeze or recovery controls exist.

entries.title: Engine
entries.identity: The runtime component that schedules and coordinates repeated market-evaluation work.
entries.purpose: It shows whether the evaluation loop is running and whether recent decision activity is observable.
entries.pipeline_position: The engine receives configuration and market inputs, invokes decision processing, and emits operational evidence; it is not itself the complete strategy or broker.
controls: Open Status or Diagnostics through the surrounding panel.
consequences: Refresh is read-only and does not restart the engine.
limitations: Running means the loop is active; it does not prove fresh data, valid signals, delivery, or profit.
Decision count measures observed processing, not successful trades.
glossary: Tick interval
The configured delay between scheduled evaluation cycles.
Last decision timestamp
The latest decision time visible to this status source.
Decision count
The number of decision records observed by the current status source.

entries.title: Strategy Parameters
entries.identity: The governed configuration surface for adjustable decision parameters.
entries.purpose: It makes current thresholds, structural-space requirements, instability gates, coverage, and profiles visible and controllable within permission boundaries.
entries.pipeline_position: Parameters influence future decision evaluation; the canonical strategy and validation layers remain their semantic owners.
controls: Inspect thresholds, S/R requirements, spike filters, active symbols, and the current profile.
Authorized mutation controls may update validated future-facing configuration.
consequences: Increasing or decreasing a parameter may change which future opportunities pass a gate.
A profile applies a governed bundle of parameter values; it does not replace the strategy.
limitations: No parameter setting guarantees signal frequency, win rate, or profit.
Parameter changes must not rewrite historical decisions or outcomes.

entries.title: Choose Strategy
entries.identity: The governed selection surface for installed trading-strategy families.
entries.purpose: It shows which trading strategy is currently selected, which canonical specification governs it, and which future strategies remain unavailable.
entries.pipeline_position: Strategy selection identifies the installed decision family before market analysis; it does not itself calculate a decision, send a signal, or execute a trade.
controls: Inspect the currently selected strategy and its canonical version.
Inspect future strategy families without activating them.
Return to Decision Visibility or Admin.
consequences: Opening or refreshing this page is read-only.
A future strategy can become selectable only after implementation, validation, and Owner approval.
limitations: Selecting or displaying a strategy does not enable signal delivery or broker execution.
No strategy can guarantee that every trade will win or produce profit.
glossary: AVAILABLE
The strategy family is installed and may be selected under its governed controls.
NOT AVAILABLE YET
The strategy is a recorded future objective and has no active decision or execution logic.

entries.title: Decision Thresholds
entries.identity: Minimum governed score boundaries for progressive decision stages.
entries.purpose: They separate early opportunity awareness from stronger confirmation and immediate actionability.
entries.pipeline_position: The decision layer compares evidence-derived scores with these thresholds before lifecycle progression.
controls: Inspect PRE, CONFIRM, and OPEN values.
Authorized roles may update a validated threshold.
consequences: A higher threshold generally requires stronger evidence and may reduce progression frequency.
A lower threshold generally allows weaker candidates to progress and may increase risk or noise.
limitations: Crossing a score threshold alone is not sufficient for OPEN_NOW; focus, timing, corridor, instability, and other gates still apply.
Thresholds do not predict or guarantee profit.
glossary: PRE
Early-stage opportunity evidence suitable for governed observation.
CONFIRM
Stronger evidence that may progress an already valid opportunity.
OPEN / OPEN_NOW
The highest actionability stage, still subject to every mandatory safety and feasibility gate.

entries.title: S/R and Corridor
entries.identity: The structural-space gate around support, resistance, and available price room.
entries.purpose: It helps reject opportunities that do not have enough usable space relative to the required movement buffer.
entries.pipeline_position: It evaluates structural actionability before a candidate may become immediately actionable.
controls: Authorized roles may update the validated multiplier.
consequences: Increasing the multiplier generally demands more structural room and is more restrictive.
Decreasing it generally accepts tighter room and may increase structural risk.
limitations: Passing the S/R gate does not prove timing feasibility or profitability.
A failed mandatory structural-space gate cannot be treated as an informal suggestion.
glossary: S/R
Support and resistance: nearby market structure used to estimate usable movement space.

entries.title: Spike and Instability Filter
entries.identity: A safety gate that identifies abnormal candle shape, range, or jump behavior.
entries.purpose: It prevents unstable price movement from being treated as an ordinary actionable setup.
entries.pipeline_position: It consumes candle and volatility evidence before final signal actionability.
controls: Inspect wick/body, range-z, and jump-versus-ATR limits.
Authorized roles may update validated limits.
consequences: Higher maxima are generally more permissive of unstable movement.
Lower maxima are generally more restrictive and may reject more candidates.
limitations: The filter reduces a defined instability risk; it cannot make a trade safe or profitable.
ATR is a volatility measure, not a direction forecast.
glossary: Wick/body ratio
Compares candle wick size with its real body.
Range z-score
Compares the current candle range with its recent statistical baseline.
Jump vs ATR
Compares a sudden move with recent average true range volatility.

entries.title: Symbols and Coverage
entries.identity: The governed universe of markets the system is allowed to monitor for future activity.
entries.purpose: It lets authorized operators inspect or change prospective market coverage without altering historical evidence.
entries.pipeline_position: Coverage is an input boundary before scanning and decision evaluation.
consequences: Enabling a symbol allows future monitoring; it does not create a signal.
Disabling a symbol removes it from future coverage and may require focus eviction, but must not rewrite history.
limitations: An active symbol is not proof of provider readiness, signal readiness, or profitability.
Coverage changes apply prospectively.

entries.title: Decision Visibility
entries.identity: A read-only explanation surface for the latest observable decision evidence.
entries.purpose: It helps an authorized human understand why a candidate passed, failed, stalled, downgraded, or was rejected.
entries.pipeline_position: It reads decision, gate, score, focus, and lifecycle evidence between market evaluation and governed distribution.
controls: Refresh the latest available decision evidence.
consequences: Inspection does not override, replay, or mutate strategy truth.
limitations: One decision snapshot is not a performance statistic.
Missing evidence must remain unknown; the panel must not invent a reason.
glossary: Score
A governed aggregation of decision evidence, not a probability of profit.
Gate
A mandatory condition that may block progression even when a score is high.
FSM
The finite-state lifecycle that governs valid progression between operational stages.

entries.title: Distribution Control
entries.identity: The routing and publication-readiness surface for already eligible outputs.
entries.purpose: It shows where a governed signal may be delivered and whether configured routes are ready.
entries.pipeline_position: It is downstream of decision/FSM eligibility and upstream of Telegram or other destination publishers.
controls: Use route mutations only when a canonical backend and permission are available.
consequences: A future route control may permit, restrict, mute, or freeze prospective publication to a destination.
limitations: Distribution does not decide whether a signal is valid.
Successful delivery does not mean the signal was profitable.
Configured route text is not proof of live end-to-end delivery.

entries.title: Research and Analytics
entries.identity: A read-only review surface for governed performance, outcome, rejection, and experiment data products.
entries.purpose: It supports evidence-based evaluation and comparison without giving analytics automatic strategy authority.
entries.pipeline_position: It consumes labeled decision, outcome, market, operational, and distribution evidence after runtime activity.
consequences: Reading or exporting a report does not change the production strategy.
limitations: Community feedback is not objective Market Truth.
A report based on incomplete evidence must not be treated as complete performance truth.
Historical performance does not guarantee future results.

entries.title: Intelligence
entries.identity: A higher-order summary of patterns, anomalies, drift, and recommendation candidates.
entries.purpose: It helps humans notice evidence that may deserve investigation or governed research.
entries.pipeline_position: It is downstream of observability and analytics and upstream of human review; it is advisory, not production authority.
consequences: A recommendation may enter review but must not automatically mutate production behavior.
limitations: A pattern or anomaly is not automatically causal.
No displayed recommendation is approval, canonical change, or profit guarantee.

entries.title: Affiliate and Partner
entries.identity: A scope-limited commercial visibility surface for referral and partner operations.
entries.purpose: It separates authorized affiliate metrics and support workflows from strategy, execution, and unrestricted admin authority.
entries.pipeline_position: It consumes commercial and distribution-adjacent evidence without owning signal validity or global routing.
controls: Inspect only the affiliate scope allowed to the current identity.
consequences: Viewing affiliate data does not grant wider admin or strategy permissions.
limitations: Affiliate roles are not strategy or distribution owners.
The surface must not expose other affiliates' private scope or internal strategy truth.

entries.title: Roles and Identity
entries.identity: The surface that explains who the current actor is and which governed role memberships apply.
entries.purpose: It makes authorization context visible and provides a controlled configuration reload where separately permitted.
entries.pipeline_position: It reads the canonical role and permission configuration used by admin command and callback enforcement.
controls: Authorized admin-topic users may reload role and permission configuration.
consequences: Reload re-reads configuration; it does not grant roles that are absent from the governed source.
limitations: Seeing a role does not bypass per-command permission checks or chat-context requirements.
Owner private chat intentionally cannot perform the role-reload mutation.

entries.title: Files and Reports
entries.identity: A bounded, permission-checked browser for operational artifacts made available by the runtime.
entries.purpose: It lets an authorized operator inspect or download evidence without treating the file browser as a source of new system truth.
entries.pipeline_position: It exposes selected observability, outcome, analytics, report, documentation, and audit artifacts produced by their owning subsystems.
consequences: Download sends a separate Telegram document and does not mutate the artifact.
limitations: An empty directory means no artifact is currently exposed there; it does not prove the underlying subsystem never ran.
Only allow-listed paths and sanitized exports may be exposed.

entries.title: Governance and Documentation
entries.identity: The discoverable reference surface for active canon, governed implementation references, and change-control evidence.
entries.purpose: It helps an authorized human locate the documents that own the meaning of the system and its controls.
entries.pipeline_position: It is a presentation layer over the active canonical documentation hierarchy.
consequences: Reading or downloading documentation does not modify canon or runtime behavior.
limitations: Deprecated, superseded, proposed, or historical documents must not be presented as active authority.
Telegram summaries do not replace the complete canonical documents.

entries.title: Diagnostics
entries.identity: A concise operational interpretation of currently available runtime evidence.
entries.purpose: It helps an authorized operator identify likely failure areas and obtain a sanitized audit artifact.
entries.pipeline_position: It consumes health, observability, recovery, and configuration evidence without replacing their canonical owners.
controls: Generate a sanitized Runtime Audit artifact.
consequences: Diagnosis and audit generation are observational; they do not repair or restart the system.
limitations: A diagnosis is bounded by available evidence and must not invent missing causes.
A generated audit is a snapshot, not a permanent guarantee of health.

entries.title: System Health and Recovery
entries.identity: The aggregated technical-health surface for runtime, market data, Telegram, FSM, recovery, and shadow state.
entries.purpose: It helps an operator distinguish healthy, degraded, blocked, unknown, and recovery-relevant conditions.
entries.pipeline_position: It consumes observability and recovery evidence and links to Engine, Diagnostics, and Runtime Audit.
consequences: These current controls inspect evidence; they do not restart or repair the service.
limitations: An overall healthy label does not prove profitable trading.
A recovery recommendation is not an executed recovery action.
Unknown evidence must remain visibly unknown.

entries.title: Security and Audit
entries.identity: The oversight surface for permission-sensitive activity, access denials, admin evidence, and sanitized audit exports.
entries.purpose: It supports accountability and forensic review of governed operations.
entries.pipeline_position: It consumes role, admin-action, observability, and audit evidence without granting mutation authority.
consequences: Audit generation creates a sanitized snapshot artifact; it does not change runtime behavior.
limitations: Audit visibility must not expose credentials, secrets, protected identities, or unrestricted payloads.
Absence of a displayed event is not proof that an event did not occur unless the canonical evidence contract says so.
